premises.text: Employers drown in low-quality applications and waste hours finding the few relevant candidates
premises.evidence_span: I spend hours sifting through the noise to find those 10 best

premises.text: Job seekers struggle to get noticed and lack feedback on whether applications were viewed or how employers reacted
premises.evidence_span: how does my resume or cover letter, the one that's spot on, the one that's perfect for the job I applied to, get noticed?

premises.text: LocalBacon handpicks quality full-time jobs in a uniform format—no MLM/scams—with dynamic search and saved jobs
premises.evidence_span: we handpick every single job that's posted on our site

premises.text: Job seekers pay to apply (starting $0.99 via job credits), which makes employers notice applications
premises.evidence_span: job seekers pay to apply on LocalBacon

premises.text: Employers agree to give feedback and notify seekers when applications are viewed; flagging can sync to ATS
premises.evidence_span: employers and recruiters agree to give feedback and allow the job seeker to know when they view their application

premises.text: Employer UI categorizes candidates (new/flagged/shelved) with familiar workflows and transparency when shelving
premises.evidence_span: we categorize candidates as new, as flagged, or as shelved

value.text: Fix fundamental hiring problems for both job seekers and employers—signal and transparency instead of noise
value.evidence_span: fix the fundamental problems that exist for both job seekers and employers

causal_links.evidence_span: job seekers pay to apply on LocalBacon. And they notice that

notes: Employer and seeker pains folded as one broken two-sided hiring problem set but split into two premises under distinct stakeholder jobs (§4.1.6/tie-break). Search/save/iPaper apply UI cascade folded into curated platform. Survey willingness-to-pay treated as evidence for pay-to-apply premise not traction metric. Transcript ends mid-wrap. Two domains—not need/product/money triad.
